title: Emberbrook — the town-wide dressing pass
subtitle: The pilot's ratified engine, run over the whole village. Every frame below is derived: no camera was aimed by eye, no placement was nudged, and where a subject stands behind the town's own planting the frame says so instead of moving it.

sections.title: The districts
sections.blurb: One eye-level frame per **map parcel** — the same parcels that derive every scene contract and sceneKey, so the district set is the map's and not this lane's. The camera stands ON THE WALK NETWORK (a district frame is a place the player can be), at the standoff the target's own built extent solves for, at the lens and the min/max distances `emberbrook.cameras.json` already ratifies. Among the candidate stands the best nine-ray clear fraction on the target wins; a frame under 60% is REPORTED occluded, not fixed by moving the town.

sections.title: Before / after, from the same camera
sections.blurb: `--nodress` runs the identical derivation with every dressing stage skipped: same map, same harvest, same light key, same shot solver, same lens, same pixel grid. The only difference between the two images is the thing being reviewed. (The two Emberbrook frame sets already on disk are 1600x914 plates solved before the 2x rescale — putting one of those beside a dressed frame would have compared two cameras, not two dressings.)

sections.title: What the frames ask you to rule on
sections.blurb: A review board's job is to put the questions in front of you, not to answer them. These are the things the town-wide frames show that this lane did NOT decide, in the order they cost the most.

rows.text: A CLEAR FRACTION IS NOT A COMPOSITION TEST, and `district-lane` is the proof.

rows: That frame is a timber wall at arm's length. The solver's own printed report, on the run that shipped it: *best stand sees it 89% clear: pond 89% (nearest blocker `lm_item-shop_body` at 6.2 m of 28.4)*. Both halves are true. Nine rays to a 6 m target disc 28 m away all thread PAST a wall 6 m in front of the camera, because that wall does not cover the TARGET — it covers the FRAME. The instrument measures the subject and says nothing at all about the picture, and it printed the 6.2 m as prose next to a 89% it treated as a pass.

mine, and the fix is as precise as the defect: a candidate stand must also clear its NEAR FIELD — reject any stand whose nearest blocker inside the frustum is closer than a stated fraction of the standoff. The number is already being printed; it just is not a criterion.

rows.text: THE HEARTLIGHT IS A WHITE CONE.

rows: `district-square` puts it in frame at eye level for the first time and `lm_heartlight_flame` renders as a hard clipped white pyramid on its plinth. This is the story's own core object -- the map's note says treat it with reverence in every shot -- and it is the one thing in the village the dressing pass deliberately did NOT touch, on the rule that a dressing layer does not re-grade the Heartlight. That rule protected it from being casually re-materialled and left it as blockout massing in the one frame the whole town is built around.
coordinator's, and it wants its own small round rather than a material row: a flame is a look decision with canon attached, not a substitution.

rows.text: And the same frame is the evidence the material pass works.

rows: Clay pantile roofs with real course pitch, lime plaster walls carrying their own weathering and moss, coursed rubble bases, timber posts, and the bell's post-and-lintel frame from the Festival Square hero kit -- all of it out of ONE table keyed on the blockout's own material names. 1247 slots, no object inspected, no placement moved.
nobody -- this is the pass landing.

rows.text: THE RIM TREES ARE BLOWN UP FROM SHRUBS, AND IT RUINS THE GAME'S FIRST GROUND.

rows: `district-woodroad` is the arrival clearing — the map calls it *THE GAME'S FIRST GROUND, where Vesper's arrival stages* — and it shows a trunk about 4 m across with root flares sprawling eight metres over the road, backed by a rank of ten visibly IDENTICAL specimens. The mechanism is in one line of `dress_forest`: a rim stand is scaled by (the blockout's proxy stand height) / (the library asset's own height), with no bound on the ratio. Where the blockout massed a 20 m stand and the picker drew a 3.2 m `searsia`, that is a **6.25x uniform scale** — and a uniform scale takes the root flare, the bark grain and the leaf cards up with it. `dress_trees` has had the answer since round 1 and calls it out in its own log line: *HEIGHT TRIMMED, NOT SCALED — the library asset is already sized for its class and object-scaling would wreck its leaf cards.* The village trees get that rule. The 321 forest trees do not.

mine. The fix is to make `dress_forest` pick an asset whose NATIVE height is near the wanted height and then bound the residual scale (the same 0.7-1.4x band the village trees already live in), rather than scaling whatever the picker drew to whatever the stand asks for. This and the lamp glass are the next round.

rows.text: And the same frame shows the forest is one asset, ten times.

rows: The rank behind the Waystone is ten instances of the same scan at the same scale with only a yaw between them. The library ships two conifers and eight broadleaf-class entries; `pick_for` draws from the class pool on a crc, so a class with one usable member repeats. Related to the row above and not the same fault: even correctly scaled, this rank would still be one silhouette.
mine, and cheaper than it looks — it is a picker-diversity question, not new assets.

rows.text: The unclaimed ring: MEASURED, and it is mostly not where the far aerial says.

rows: Read off `aerial-south` alone this looked like the farmland ruling's unexecuted stamp — a wood standing off the houses with bare ground between. A 2 m plan census of the master says otherwise. Canopy as DISCS (crown corner over root two, not bounding boxes — 887 yawed crown AABBs read as 99% coverage of a valley that is half open, which is the same instrument error this pass refuted for `walk_pad_pips-den`): **wood 29,860 m2 = 75% of the valley, open 7,820 m2 = 20%, water 4%, built footprint 1%.** Ground that is open AND enclosed by the wood in 6 of 8 directions within 50 m — i.e. actually *between* the village and the treeline — is **416 m2, 1%, and there is no contiguous parcel over 300 m2.** `aerial-core` shows the same thing by eye: the wood presses right in between the houses, which is the coexistence ruling holding.

the open tan the far aerial shows is OUTSIDE the wood ring, on plateau the forest ruling itself says to swallow with more forest, and which no plate camera at maxDist 46 m can reach. Coordinator's, but the farmland stamp has less to execute than one frame suggested.

rows.text: EVERY LAMP GLASS IN EVERY EYE-LEVEL FRAME CLIPS TO PURE WHITE.

rows: `district-entrance`, `district-homerow` and `district-square` all show it: the lantern's emissive glass box renders as a featureless blown white rectangle with no form, no falloff and no visible fixture. It is the same family as carried redline (a) — 680 W behind a 0.30 m glass box — but where (a) is about a SURFACE the lamp over-lights 5.9 m away, this is the FIXTURE ITSELF, in the near field, in every frame a player will stand in. Fourteen of these are the one thing this town has that no other town in the world does, and right now each one is a white rectangle.

mine, and it displaces the material work at the top of my next round. `--lampclamp` is in the engine and defaulted off; the measurement is an emb_lum box on the glass itself, which no round has taken yet.

rows.text: The implied-scale massing reads as white and orange slabs, and it is the biggest thing in two frames.

rows: `far-rooftops-nw`, `hillside-cottages` and `east-cottages` render as untextured white-and-orange stepped blocks with black patches, and in `aerial-east` they are visually larger than the village they are supposed to imply is beyond it. Two separate faults: the material pass re-surfaced 1247 slots town-wide and did not reach these, and their massing scale reads as towers rather than as a further tier of cottage roofs.
the material half is mine, next round. The SCALE half is blockout-side and is the one that actually costs the frame.
The valley ground sheet has a visible edge.

An aerial at 394 m sees the whole of `emb_ground_valley` and its cliff edge, with black beyond. No plate camera ever does — `maxDist` is 46 m. The aerials are a survey instrument and this is what a survey instrument shows; it is recorded so nobody reads it as a defect in the town.
nobody — reported so it is not re-found.
The Heartlight reads, and it reads first.

At 394 m and at eye level the Heartlight's glow is the brightest thing in the village and the lamps ring it. That is the story's own claim about this town made visible, and it came for free out of canon lighting nobody re-graded.
nobody — this one is just true.
The open tan BEYOND the wood ring is a taste question, not a stamp.

The census puts 7,820 m2 (20% of the valley) of open ground outside the wood's ring, on plateau. The standing forest ruling's default is that the wood swallows it. The alternative -- visible worked land beyond the treeline -- is a look choice nobody has made. No plate camera at maxDist 46 m reaches any of it either way.
the user's. Routed here rather than into a rebuild.
The Old Gate court's kit is in frame and not readable.

The map's note requires the two CH1 sigil plates IN FRAME, and they are — built proud of the apron at their stamped coordinates, 87 hero-kit pieces in all. At the standoff the solver picks for `gate-court` they subtend about two pixels each, and the 63 flagstones read as one flat grey apron rather than as paving. The kit is correct and the frame is too far back for it.
the cameras lane's, not the kit's. Recorded here because 'in frame' is not 'readable' and this town has a canon document about exactly that distinction.
sections.note: The dressing lane fixed six rules this pass and did not touch the map, the cameras, the blockout's massing or the lighting grade.

sections.title: What the town broke, and what it cost
sections.blurb: Five failure classes the pilot could not have found at 30 m. Each was fixed in the RULE, never in the output, and each row carries the instrument that named it.
rows: `RR = 1e9` was a sentinel, and three rules spend it as a **length**
`dress_bank_planting` drew 260 candidates from a square of side 2xRR about the region centre, then kept the ones within 3.40 m of water
town-wide: **0 plants**, reported as success. Same code at the mill: 176

the region is the map's own landmark extent (centre 64.0, 56.0, radius 104 m); candidates are drawn around **each water body's own bounds**. Town-wide now **1112 plants from 1298 candidates, 86% accepted**
700 clumps/m2 is a density, and over a valley it is also a budget
one particle system for the whole request. Blender's `distribute_particles` sorts it in a **single-threaded** `BLI_qsort_r`
**2256 of 2257** stack samples inside nested qsort frames, 11 GB resident, **no output in 15 minutes**. 39,237 m2 x 700 = **27.5M particles**

the scatter is spent inside a **14 m band about the walk network** (9,546 of 39,237 m2 = 24.3%) because the plates are composed on the lanes; the request is tiled at 400k per system with crc-derived per-slab seeds. **6.68M over 17 slabs**, density unchanged
the ground oracle went through the **depsgraph**
`raycast_ground` called `Object.ray_cast`, which needs the EVALUATED mesh — and every `veg()` call creates an object, which TAGS the depsgraph. One realize of every instance so far, per placement

`execute_realize_mesh_tasks` + `adapt_mesh_domain_face_to_point` + `threaded_copy` at **100% of samples for over an hour**, part way through placements. It never looked like a hang because it was never idle

a standalone `BVHTree` over the ground's world-space verts, rebuilt only by the two stages that cut it. **No depsgraph in the oracle at all.** The same build reached bank planting and groundcover in minutes
the shot **solver** paid for the scatter on every ray
the build finished and the solver hung, which looks identical from outside. Each candidate stand costs one ground ray and one nine-ray census
same realize signature, hundreds of rays

the groundcover particle modifiers leave the depsgraph for the solve and for the hero kits, and go back **before a pixel is traced**. A 0.4 m clump was never an occluder at 12-46 m and `_cast_visible` already skipped hidden hits
the town had **no building layer at all**
outside the mill's own 670-line kit, all 999 `lm_` meshes rendered as flat gray massing. `hide_gray` had been hiding this at the pilot's 30 m radius; at `--region all` it correctly turns itself off
2,232 objects in the master; the dressing touched 555 instances and one corner

the blockout **already names every surface it paints** — `emb_mat_thatch`, `_plaster`, `_stone`, `_timber`, `_cobble` — exactly as the 21/29/15 crown recipes name a species. The dressing re-renders its MATERIAL CLASSES once. Heartlight, lamp glass, windows and water are excluded on stated rules
`masonry_scanned` could only fall back to **grey**
a missing role fell through to `masonry()`'s coursed procedural grey
with `roof_thatch` absent, every roof in Emberbrook would have become coursed stone — silently
`fb_mat` names the honest fallback per role; five CC0 roles were then intaken so none of them is needed
sections.note: Instruments: tools/emb_lum.py (the ruler), tools/dressing_texmeasure.py (the library's albedo ruler), macOS `sample` on the stalled process (the qsort and the realize), and the engine's own printed census.
